key_insight: SegviGen repurposes pretrained 3D generative models as structural priors to produce accurate part-level segmentations without training large 3D discriminative models or relying on noisy multi-view mask aggregation.
problem_solved: Addresses inconsistent, blurred, or annotation-heavy 3D part segmentation pipelines by leveraging the inherent structure in pretrained 3D generators to obtain coherent, fine-grained part labels with far less 3D supervision.
method: Extract structured shape and appearance priors from a pretrained 3D generative model to reveal consistent part cues across samples and views.
Map generative features to part labels via lightweight procedures (e.g., latent perturbation, feature clustering, or small-scale label propagation) instead of training a large discriminative network.
Optionally refine segmentation with minimal supervision or small optimization steps to improve boundary accuracy and cross-view consistency.
impact: Enables practitioners to get high-quality 3D part segmentations with far lower annotation and training cost, improving scalability for downstream tasks like editing, simulation, and robotics.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained 3D generator → feature extraction → part labeling → refinement
Before/After comparison: multi-view aggregation baseline vs. SegviGen segmented model highlighting sharper boundaries
Latent/feature-space visualization: clusters corresponding to semantic parts
Bar chart: annotation/time/training cost reduction compared to fully supervised 3D segmentation
paper_title: SegviGen: Repurposing 3D Generative Model for Part Segmentation
paper_authors: Lin Li, Haoran Feng, Zehuan Huang, Haohua Chen, Wenbo Nie
